text:
The Waeslefell Compact’s twenty-year span from 22 to 41 was defined by a violent succession and a protracted war that ended in territorial gain but internal collapse. The period began with Vaell Foull holding the seat, a rule that ended when Ground Raeskur had him murdered at Skomere in 24. Ground Raeskur took the seat by right of birth and held it for nine years, during which the Compact engaged in a war with the Baesveireach Compact that lasted four years. The Compact lost one battle at Thea Seam in 26 but won three others, taking Thea Seam and Baesveireach from its enemy. Ground Raeskur’s rule ended in 32 when Fur Roundpoull challenged him openly and won the seat.

Fur Roundpoull ruled for one year before dying in Waeslefell in 33. Rontaen Sin took the seat by setting aside the claim of the named heir Rearn Thill, dividing the Compact and losing Baesveireach to Greater Baesveireach. Rontaen Sin was murdered by Nounmam Mith in 36. Deththou Keis took the seat by right of birth but was cast out in 37 when Nounmam Mith won a coup. Nounmam Mith held the seat until the end of the period. Throughout these years, the Compact sent two raids that carried off plunder and suffered nine raids, all of which were beaten off. It fought five battles, winning four and losing one.

The Compact’s standing deteriorated significantly. In 35, Thea Seam rose against it because its standing had fallen to nothing. Six years of hunger at Thea Seam killed 23 people and caused 60 to flee. The Compact declared war on the Deafil League in 34, defeating it and taking Skomere, which led to the Deafil League’s destruction. It also made peace with the Baesveireach Compact after that power collapsed. Nine people were courted away from its rulers. Four people were cast out, three were murdered from within, and one was declared outlaw. The period ended with Nounmam Mith still holding the seat, but the Compact had lost two places and seen its internal cohesion break down.

The Skomere Charter’s tenure began in 47 with a rupture in the Waeslefell Compact. Touthseand Gourses carried off two places from the Waeslefell Compact to establish the Skomere Charter, shifting the balance of power in the region. This act of division marked the start of the period, with Gourses holding the seat as the new power took shape.

The period remained stable under Gourses’s rule, with no further challenges to his authority recorded. The Skomere Charter held its ground, defined by the initial seizure rather than subsequent expansion or conflict. The power existed as a distinct entity, separate from the Waeslefell Compact, but its internal structure and external relations remained unchanged throughout the years.

The period ended in 51 with the return of exiles to the Skomere Charter. Nounmam Mith returned from exile in 50 and took service with the Skomere Charter. Meirnhaes Kould returned from exile in 51 and also took service with the Skomere Charter. These returns did not alter the seat’s holder, but they marked the close of the period with the reintegration of former outsiders into the Charter’s service.

The Waeslefell Compact’s twenty-year span from 2 to 21 was defined by a war of attrition against the Baesveireach Compact and the slow collapse of its internal authority. At the start, the Compact held Fa Cut, a site it had occupied in 2. Its standing eroded through six consecutive defeats at Thea Seam between 4 and 9, where it lost 87 men in total. The conflict began in 4 when the Compact declared war on the Baesveireach Compact for Thea Seam, breaking an alliance formed in 3 by the marriage of Vaell Foull and Freallball Fisu. The war ended in 10 with both sides exhausted, but the Compact had already suffered famine at Fa Cut and raids on Waeslefell and Weisfaewick.

Leadership shifted three times as the seat passed from Keirn Heapound, who died in 10, to Vaell Foull, who took the seat by right of birth. Vaell’s rule was marked by internal dissent; Grefraem Meheath was cast out in 11 for attempted murder and conspiracy. In 13, Vor Saern challenged Vaell openly, won, and took the seat. Vaell was cast out, and Fa Cut rose against the Compact, whose standing had fallen to nothing. Vor Saern ruled until his death in 17, when Vaell Foull took the seat again by right of birth and held it at the end of the period.

The Compact’s power was further diminished by eight years of hunger and sickness that killed 302 people and drove 147 from their homes. It sent four raids that carried off plunder but suffered ten raids, only four of which were beaten off. The period ended with Vaell Foull still holding the seat, but the Compact had lost all its external alliances, suffered massive casualties in its war with the Baesveireach Compact, and seen its own people flee or die from disease and starvation.

The Waeslefell Compact endured a decade of violent succession and territorial collapse, beginning with a contested leadership and ending with the death of its final ruler. The period opened with Greandsam Kreir seizing the seat from Nounmam Mith in 42, a transfer marked by open challenge and exile. Kreir’s rule was short-lived; he was murdered at Skomere in 47 by Thraebaern Ramdem, an act that coincided with the death of steward Sealdvern Geitoun. The power fractured immediately after, losing Skomere to the Skomere Charter and seeing Noulldou Beivourn take the seat by setting aside the named heir Touthseand Gourses.

Instability persisted as Woum Teldlei defeated Beivourn in 48, only to be killed by Feinnind Keitrith two years later. Ronith Wasnur then seized the seat, also by setting aside a named heir, and ruled until his death in 51. His tenure was marked by internal purges; Gandkim Kiveald and Full Sanweil were cast out for conspiracies against him, and Kiveald was declared an outlaw. The Compact’s standing had fallen to nothing by 48, evidenced by Fa Cut rising against it, and it suffered plague at Skomere that killed 176 people.

The period closed with Haeth Tha taking the seat in 51, setting aside Thraebaern Ramdem. Over the ten years, six people held the seat: two were cast out, two were killed, one died, and one remained in power. The Compact sent one raid, which carried off plunder, and suffered three raids, all beaten off. It lost two places to the Skomere Charter and formed one marriage alliance with Free Kremoor. The era ended with the seat held by Haeth Tha, following the death of Ronith Wasnur.

The Deafil League spent thirty-four years bound to the Baesveireach Compact through four marriages, yet ended its existence defeated by the Waeslefell Compact. At the start of the period, the League held Skomere and maintained a fragile alliance with Waeslefell, but its standing deteriorated rapidly. By year 24, Kremoor rose against it as its authority fell very low, and by year 28, Kremoor broke away entirely as Free Kremoor. The League’s final years were marked by internal purges and a single war that it lost, resulting in the loss of Skomere and the scattering of its followers.

Feasleith Husbill held the seat until his death in year 11, after which Steapall Faedild took power by setting aside the named heir Bage Busba. Faedild’s rule was challenged openly by Fur Roundpoull in year 23; Faedild lost the seat and was cast out. Fur Roundpoull then ruled until year 28, when Sealdvern Geitoun challenged him and took the seat by coup. Geitoun’s rule lasted only one year before he was cast out for an attempted murder on Ground Raeskur. Deththou Keis then took the seat by setting aside the named heir Touthseand Gourses, holding power until the League’s end.

The League sent eight raids against the Waeslefell Compact between years 8 and 31. Two raids in years 8 and 9 carried off plunder from Waeslefell and Weisfaewick respectively. One raid in year 10 got through to Fa Cut but took nothing. Five subsequent raids in years 17, 18, 19, 30, and 31 were beaten off. The League suffered four raids from the Waeslefell Compact in years 8, 9, 18, and 19, all of which carried off plunder from Kremoor and Skomere. In year 34, the Waeslefell Compact declared war on the League over a long-standing grievance, broke its alliance, and defeated the League at Skomere, killing 179 and taking the settlement. The League was finished in year 34, landless, with its last four followers scattering.

The Baesveireach Compact’s twenty-seven years were defined by a single, exhausting quarrel with the Waeslefell Compact. The conflict began in year 4 when Waeslefell declared war over Thea Seam and broke its alliance with Baesveireach. Baesveireach and its allies won seven battles against Waeslefell at Thea Seam between years 4 and 9, inflicting 87 deaths. They raided Waeslefell in year 6, taking 30 grain and killing 59. Raids on Weisfaewick in year 7 and Fa Cut in year 8 were beaten off. Peace was made in year 10 after six years of war.

Internal instability weakened the Compact. Sildbeld Bouthwoun died in year 13. Kramboul Dend took the seat by strongest claim, setting aside the named heir Fur Roundpoull, who was cast out. Kramboul died in year 18. Bage Busba took the seat by strongest claim. Thea Seam rose against Baesveireach in year 16 as its standing fell very low. A plague broke out at Baesveireach in year 21, killing 213 people. In year 22, 179 died and 224 fled. In year 23, 114 died and 143 fled.

War resumed in year 26 when Waeslefell declared war. Baesveireach won one battle but lost three. Waeslefell took Thea Seam in year 27 and Baesveireach in year 29. Steapall Faedild murdered Bage Busba in year 28 and took the seat, setting aside the named heir Drourn Nethi, who was cast out. Steapall was killed by Ground Raeskur in year 29. Waeslefell raided Baesveireach in year 29, taking 55 grain and killing 10. Peace was made in year 30 after the collapse of the Baesveireach Compact.

Free Kremoor spent its twenty-four years as a fragile entity, born from the Deafil League in 28 and sustained only by the loyalty of exiles and the weakness of its neighbors. Feinnind Keitrith held the seat from the beginning, ruling for five years before his own attempt on Greandsam Kreir failed in 44. His rule ended when he was cast out for attempted murder, and Nounmam Mith took the seat by election. Nounmam Mith’s tenure lasted five years until he too was cast out for attempted murder in 49. Til Saeld then took the seat, which he still held when the period ended in 51. The seat passed from one person to another two times inside this period.

The power was defined by its reliance on men returning from exile. Seven exiles returned to take service with Free Kremoor during these years. Staellou Keillthae returned in 29 and challenged Feinnind Keitrith openly in 35. He lost the challenge, and Feinnind Keitrith kept the seat. Staellou Keillthae was then killed by Feinnind Keitrith at Kremoor in 35. Sealdvern Geitoun returned in 34 and attempted Feinnind Keitrith’s life in 39. He was cast out for attempted murder in 39. His conspiracy against the seat was uncovered in 40, and he was declared outlaw.

Free Kremoor’s external relations were marked by failed aggression and shifting alliances. It sent out five raids, all of which were beaten off. The raids targeted Thea Seam in 34, Fa Cut in 35, Waeslefell in 37, Skomere in 38, and Fa Cut again in 51. All five raids were directed against the Waeslefell Compact. Free Kremoor swore an alliance with the Deafil League in 29 and with Greater Baesveireach in 35. Ground Raeskur abandoned Free Kremoor for the Waeslefell Compact in 37. Touthseand Gourses abandoned Free Kremoor for the Waeslefell Compact in 40. Sealdvern Geitoun won Deththou Keis away from Feinnind Keitrith in 38. Free Kremoor ordered zero killings against people of other powers. One of its own people was murdered from within. Three people were cast out for attempted murder. One person already gone was declared outlaw.

The period from 33 to 51 saw Greater Baesveireach shift from a state of territorial expansion to one of internal consolidation and external vulnerability. At the start, Rearn Thill held the seat and expanded the power’s reach by taking two places from the Waeslefell Compact in 33. The power’s standing was defined by its inability to project force outward, as all four raids it sent out between 38 and 43 were beaten off by the Waeslefell Compact. Simultaneously, the power suffered two raids by the Waeslefell Compact in 41 and 42, which carried off plunder from Baesveireach and Weisfaewick.

Rearn Thill’s rule ended in 48 when he was killed by Feinnind Keitrith at Baesveireach. Feinnind Keitrith had returned from exile in 45 and taken service with the power, then murdered Sealdvern Geitoun at Waeslefell in 47. Feinnind Keitrith took the seat by right of birth and remained holding it through the end of the period. His rule was marked by internal purges, including the murder of Woum Teldlei at Waeslefell in 49.

The power finished the period with Feinnind Keitrith still holding the seat. Three exiles returned to take service with Greater Baesveireach during these years: Feinnind Keitrith in 45, Noulldou Beivourn in 49, and Full Sanweil in 51. The seat passed from one person to another one time inside this period. The power sustained two raids it suffered and sent out four raids, all of which were beaten off.

Til Saeld assumed the seat of Free Kremoor in 49, following the casting out of Nounmam Mith. Mith’s attempt on the life of Woum Teldlei had failed and been traced back to him, leading to his expulsion. With no claimant remaining, Saeld was raised from Kremoor to take the seat.

The period ended in 51 when Free Kremoor’s raid on Fa Cut was beaten off.

In year 51, Ronith Wasnur, the ruler of the Waeslefell Compact, died in Waeslefell. Haeth Tha contested the claim of Thraebaern Ramdem, the named heir, to the seat of the Waeslefell Compact. Haeth Tha took the seat, setting aside the claim of Thraebaern Ramdem.

Thraebaern Ramdem was cast out of the Waeslefell Compact. In the same year, a raid by Free Kremoor on Fa Cut was beaten off.

The war began in year 4 when the Waeslefell Compact declared war on the Baesveireach Compact for control of Thea Seam. The Baesveireach Compact and its allies defeated the Waeslefell Compact at Thea Seam in year 4, with 26 dead. The Baesveireach Compact and its allies defeated the Waeslefell Compact at Thea Seam in year 5, with 20 dead. The Baesveireach Compact and its allies defeated the Waeslefell Compact at Thea Seam in year 6, with 13 dead. The Baesveireach Compact and its allies defeated the Waeslefell Compact at Thea Seam in year 7, with 11 dead. The Baesveireach Compact and its allies defeated the Waeslefell Compact at Thea Seam in year 8, with 9 dead. The Baesveireach Compact and its allies defeated the Waeslefell Compact at Thea Seam in year 9, with 8 dead.

The conflict ended in year 10 when the Waeslefell Compact and the Baesveireach Compact made peace after 6 years, both sides exhausted.

In 26, the Waeslefell Compact declared war on the Baesveireach Compact over a long-standing grievance. The Baesveireach Compact and its allies defeated the Waeslefell Compact at Thea Seam, where 36 died. In 27, the Waeslefell Compact defeated the Baesveireach Compact at Thea Seam, where 30 died, and took the site from the Baesveireach Compact.

In 28, the Waeslefell Compact defeated the Baesveireach Compact at Baesveireach, where 82 died. In 29, Ground Raeskur had Steapall Faedild murdered at Baesveireach. Later that year, the Waeslefell Compact defeated the Baesveireach Compact at Baesveireach, where 66 died, and took the settlement from the Baesveireach Compact.

In 30, the Waeslefell Compact and the Baesveireach Compact made peace after 4 years, following the collapse of the Baesveireach Compact.
